headline: Public Divided Over New Requirement To Carry Physical Constitution To Every Grocery Store And Vegetable Market
body:
“I tried buying a kilo of onions, but the vendor refused to weigh them until I could prove the transaction was in accordance with the fundamental rights mentioned in Article 21,” said a local resident and IT consultant.

“My neighborhood sabzi-wala has started asking me to interpret the 42nd Amendment before he lets me bargain on the price of ladyfingers,” remarked a retired school teacher.

“The line at the kirana store is taking three hours now because everyone is busy debating the spirit of the Preamble just to exchange a packet of biscuits,” noted a college student.

“Honestly, the pocket-sized Constitution is just getting in the way of my grocery bag, but I suppose it beats having to explain my civil liberties to the guy selling coriander,” admitted a daily wage laborer.

“I’ve started carrying a bookmark for the Directive Principles so I can flip to the relevant page whenever the local dairy shop owner challenges my right to select the freshest milk pouch,” shared a young professional.
caption: The Constitution is the only thing we're carrying to the sabzi-wala these days. Are you reading your Preamble before buying your onions? #Constitution #MarketLife #RightsAndVeggies #Democracy (satire)
igHook: Would you actually carry your copy of the Constitution to the grocery store today?
imagePrompt: A close-up shot of a worn, pocket-sized Constitution book resting on a wooden vegetable stall next to a bunch of fresh greens and a weighing scale.

sourceHeadline.title: Democracy should function under Constitution, elections should be fair: Murli Manohar Joshi

judgeVerdict.reasoning: Candidate 4 feels the most grounded and 'human,' creating a funny, specific image of everyday citizens struggling with a nonsensical bureaucratic mandate. It avoids the 'tech-slop' tropes (like AI, PDFs, or vending machines) found in other entries, and uses the 'onion buying' detail to create a perfect, mundane clash between high constitutional law and low-stakes grocery shopping.

safetyVerdict.reasoning: The article uses the premise of carrying a Constitution to market to satirize bureaucratic absurdity and civic discourse in a harmless, non-defamatory way. It does not name private individuals, public figures, or target any specific religion, caste, or ethnicity. The image prompt is generic and does not violate the leakage policy.
